text:
anya: Quick callout — sample Edge repo broke during workshop. Worker error: 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'. Editor also shows SDK methods typed as any.
lucas: That combo usually means the bundler picked the CJS export. Which import are you using?
anya: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` in a Cloudflare Worker.
mo: Check package.json exports and tsconfig.moduleResolution. If moduleResolution is 'node' some bundlers resolve to the require target.
anya: tsconfig currently: module=ESNext, moduleResolution=node.
doc-bot: Recommended quick fixes: set moduleResolution to 'bundler' and add a worker-specific export in package.json. Example exports: "exports": { "./": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }, "./worker": { "import": "./dist/esm/worker-entry.mjs" } }.
lucas: On types: our d.ts had multiple overloads; fallback returned unknown which makes inference collapse to any. Short-term annotate call sites: `await client.call<MyType>(...)`. Long-term we should switch to a single generic signature with default = JsonValue.
mo: I patched the sample app: changed moduleResolution to 'bundler' and added ./worker export. Worker runs now; types better but I still annotated one call. Filed follow-ups: #922 (worker export), #923 (typing overload cleanup), #924 (sample README snippet).
ci-bot: CI: edge-integration job failed earlier — linked #922.
anya: Thanks. I'll add a short troubleshooting note in onboarding: set moduleResolution: 'bundler', prefer `@redwood-inference/sdk/worker` when running on edge, and pin the patched SDK once PRs land.
